title: Latency Sentiment Index & Alert Triage Playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a combined metric+trace signal and an operational triage playbook that reduces noisy latency pages by 60% while preserving high-fidelity burn-rate alerts. Implement a lightweight 'Latency Sentiment Index' (LSI) that fuses tail latency histograms, request error trends, and sampled trace anomaly scores to drive paging decisions and tiered automation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) LSI proto metric materialized in metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OTLP) with <30s freshness and documented schema.
2) Trace hook added to request router that emits a small enrichment header for 1 in N requests and feeds sparse trace ingestion.
3) New burn-rate alert rule uses LSI as a gating signal; when LSI < threshold, burn-rate opens a Slack-only channel instead of pager.
4) Triage playbook drafted and validated with oncall rotation in a 1-week dry run (runbook links + handoff steps).
5) End-to-end dashboard created in Console showing LSI, histogram slices, representative traces, and alerting state.
6) Post-launch measurement shows at least 40% reduction in pages classified as 'noise' during steady-state traffic and <5% missed high-severity incidents in simulated faults.
technical_notes:
- LSI composition: weighted sum of p95/p99 delta (30m vs 5m), error-rate derivative, and trace-anomaly z-score. Weights tunable via feature flags.
- Sparse tracing: route emits X-Obs-Sparse header and samples 1/1000 of requests for full span capture; header used by ingest to stitch sparse spans to existing request id.
- Metrics path: OTLP -> metrics-raw -> windowed-aggregator -> LSI metric with tags (region, model-route, customer-tier). Use existing aggregation infra with a dedicated aggregators config.
- Alerting rules: add gating rules in alerting engine to consult LSI and recent trace-sample density before paging. Implement a grace window for autosilencing when LSI degrades slowly.
- Backfill: run LSI offline on last 90 days to derive thresholds; store baseline percentiles per-route.
- Privacy/KMS: Ensure sampled traces are redacted server-side before storage; follow existing PII redaction guidelines.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary, 1 week): generate LSI for a subset of routes (low-risk internal routes) and expose dashboard to SRE.
Phase 2 (dry-run, 1 week): wire alert rules in dry-run mode (no pager) and route alert notifications to '#obs-triage' Slack channel. Collect false-positive/false-negative labels.
Phase 3 (controlled rollout, 2 weeks): enable gated burn-rate paging for customer-tier=internal, with manual oncall override.
Phase 4 (GA): enable for customer-tier=public with monitoring and rollback policy.
Rollback: revert alert gating config and disable sparse tracing header at proxy layer; metric aggregator supports per-route disable flags.
